heroBody: A multi cooker is one of the most-used small appliances in a US kitchen: pressure cook, slow cook, sauté, steam, yoghurt, rice and a dozen one-touch programmes in a single pot, with safety valves and timers that do the thinking for you. The US market is shaped by the Instant Pot brand family (Instant Brands continues to lead with the Instant Pot, Instant Pot Pro and Instant Pot Duo lines), the Crock-Pot brand-name slow-cooker legacy now reimagined as a multi-cooker, and a long tail of Ninja, Cosori and Breville lines at the premium end. This page pulls live US listings from BuyWhere's catalog every few minutes so the price on each card is what Amazon, Walmart, Target and Best Buy are actually charging right now, not a static snapshot from earlier in the year.

highlightSectionTitle: What changed with US multi cookers in 2026

highlights.title: The Instant Pot brand is recovering after the bankruptcy
highlights.body: Instant Brands filed for Chapter 11 in 2023, and the brand was acquired by a new owner that has re-staged the Instant Pot line at lower prices than the 2022 peak. Today's Instant Pot Duo and Instant Pot Pro at Amazon and Walmart undercut what they cost three years ago, and the lineup is more focused. If you have been waiting for a deal, the current US prices on this page are among the best in three years.

highlights.title: Air-fryer lids turned the multi cooker into a two-in-one
highlights.body: Crisping lids that snap onto a multi cooker pressure pot and turn it into an air fryer have caught on with US shoppers who own one appliance not three. Ninja Foodi, Instant Pot Air Fryer Lid and several Ultrean models now ship pressure + air fry in a single pot. This drops kitchen counter clutter and saves cabinet space, the two biggest US complaints about small kitchen appliances.

highlights.title: Walmart Everyday Low Price is the US floor
highlights.body: Unlike the Asian market where Shopee and Lazada set the floor, US multi cooker pricing is anchored on Walmart's Everyday Low Price and Amazon's daily price. Target's Circle 360 sales and Best Buy's weekend drops occasionally undercut both. Outside of Black Friday through Cyber Monday, the live listing you see here is the current US floor.

adviceSectionTitle: How to pick a multi cooker in the US without overspending
advicePoints: Buy 6-quart for two people, 8-quart for a family of four. The size jump is the most common US regret; going too small means you cook in batches on Sundays, going too large means the pot doesn't reach pressure cleanly on small weeknight meals.

Pick stainless inner pot over non-stick for daily use. Non-stick inserts wear faster in a pressure cooker than in a regular pan and replacement pots are expensive. Stainless cleans up well with a scrub and lasts the life of the machine.

Get a sealing ring spare in the first six months. The silicone sealing ring on every multi cooker absorbs the smell of whatever you cooked last; pressure cookers lose pressure slowly if the ring is saturated. Buy a second ring in a different color for savoury vs sweet so you never confuse the two.

Use Amazon Subscribe and Save for accessories. Replacement silicone rings, sealing gaskets and glass lids show up as Subscribe and Save-eligible on Amazon for a 5-15 percent discount. Set it up after you cook the first month.

Compare wattage not just programme count. A 1000W multi cooker reaches pressure noticeably faster than a 700W one, which matters on weeknight dinners where you're starting at 6 pm. Premium brands specify real wattage; budget brands sometimes don't.
faqSectionTitle: Multi cookers in the US — common questions

faqs.question: Is Instant Pot still the best multi cooker brand in the US?
faqs.answer: Yes for the value tier (Duo, Pro, Ultra). For premium US shoppers, Ninja Foodi combines pressure and air fry in one pot and is worth the step up. Crock-Pot rebranded its slow cookers as multi cookers and prices competitively, but the Instant Pot ecosystem of recipes, accessories and replacement parts remains the deepest in the US market.

faqs.question: Is an 8-quart multi cooker too big for two people?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. 8-quart pots need at least two cups of liquid to reach pressure safely, and small portions don't cook evenly in the extra space. For a household of two, 6-quart is the right pick. Go to 8-quart only if you batch cook on Sundays or feed a family of four or more.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest day to buy a multi cooker in the US?
faqs.answer: Black Friday through Cyber Monday in late November is the deepest sale window, with Prime Day in July the second. Walmart's rollback events and Target's Circle weeks add another 10-20 percent off in shoulder months. Outside of these, the live listing here is the current US floor.

faqs.question: Can a multi cooker replace a slow cooker and a rice cooker?
faqs.answer: Yes, both. Every modern multi cooker has a slow-cook mode (4-10 hours on low or high) and a rice-cook mode that handles white, brown and basmati. If you own a multi cooker and a separate slow cooker or rice cooker, you can consolidate the duplicate appliances and free a cabinet.

categoryIntro.heading: Why multi cooker prices in the US swing so widely
categoryIntro.body: Multi cookers in the US are sold by Amazon (Sold by Amazon itself plus third-party sellers), Walmart, Target and Best Buy at competitive authorized prices, plus a long tail of marketplace sellers on Amazon and eBay. Authorized retailer listings carry the manufacturer's US warranty with free shipping; marketplace sellers frequently drop the price 15-25 percent below authorized, often at the cost of a US warranty card and direct US service. The spread for the same model can reach 30 percent, which is why a static 'best price' table goes stale within days and why this page reads live listings instead.
